issues.claim: One restriction remained: an interface cannot hold instance state. It cannot declare an instance field, an auto-implemented property with backing storage or an instance constructor.
issues.problem: This restriction is the question's core claim, and neither fetched excerpt states it. The interface keyword excerpt only lists the allowed members, including 'Static fields', and says nothing explicit about instance fields. The default-interface-methods tutorial excerpt does not cover it either. The version attributions (C# 8 for private members and static fields, C# 11 for static abstract) also do not appear in the excerpts. I believe the claims are correct, but the cited pages do not show them.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a source that states it, such as https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/fundamentals/types/interfaces. That page says instance fields and instance auto-properties are not permitted in interfaces. Add the matching linkTitles entry in both locales. Alternatively, confirm that the interface keyword page states the restriction in the part of the page that was cut off.
